# My plan for this year

Well, let me think about what I'm doing this year. I'm 53, been farming these 6 mu for a long time now. My husband and our grown son do some work in town, so most of the field work falls on me. That's just how it is.

I have my land split in two pieces, more or less. About **3 mu I put into stevia** a couple of years back — the company comes and buys the dried leaves, and the price has been okay, better than just grain. Stevia is a lot of work, especially at harvest, but it brings in real money. Since it's already planted (it keeps coming back for a few years), I don't start from scratch. I just manage it this spring and through the cuts.

The **other 3 mu is wheat and then maize**, same as everyone in the village does. The wheat is already in the ground — I planted it back in October. Now in April I need to watch it, topdress some urea, and water it. After I combine the wheat in early June, I turn right around and plant maize. There's no time to rest the ground — my neighbor says three days is all he leaves between wheat harvest and maize planting, and that's about what I do too.

**For fertilizer**, I keep it simple. One bag of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) at planting, then urea to topdress. I don't measure kilograms exactly — one bag per mu for compound at base, then maybe half a bag of urea later. For stevia I have to put fertilizer after every cut, three cuts, so it eats more fertilizer than the grain fields. Stevia also wants some extra potash — the agro-store man told me that years ago and I've done it ever since.

**Water** — the well is shared with three neighbors. In a normal year I water wheat two or three times in spring (jointing, heading, grain-fill). Maize usually gets one or two waterings if July is dry. Stevia I water after each cut because the new shoots need it. Pumping costs money though, about 30–40 yuan each time per mu, so I don't water if it's going to rain.

**Pesticide** — I spray what I have to, not more. For wheat I do one spray for aphids and a herbicide in fall after planting. For maize I spray herbicide at the start and watch for armyworm. Stevia doesn't get much trouble but sometimes I spot-spray.

**Seeds** — same wheat variety as last year, Jimai 22 I think, it did okay. Maize I buy hybrid seed from the shop — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop owner recommends that's similar. I don't save seed for maize, everyone knows hybrid doesn't work the second year.

**Labor** — it's mainly me. My daughter-in-law helps during stevia harvest and wheat harvest; I pay a couple of relatives a few days for the stevia cuts since it all has to come off in a short window. Machinery I hire — combine for wheat, the planter man for maize, same guys as every year.

I'm not going to do anything fancy this year. Costs keep going up but grain prices don't really move. I can't afford to waste fertilizer, but I also can't afford to skimp and lose yield. I do about what worked last year.
